news.title: THOUSANDS of soccer fans broke a record exchanging FIFA World Cup stickers!
news.lede: An Italian company named Panini has been making awesome football-themed sticker albums since 1970 – that’s over 50 years ago! – all decorated with images of your beloved superstar strikers and goalies… And since then, collectors have traded them for the chance to finally get their favourite squad! The packages come in blind boxes with limited availability, encouraging friendly competition between fans – especially during the FIFA World Cup! So on 12 July, soccer and sticker fans from all over North America had the chance to take part in the world’s largest sports sticker exchange in 8 hours (multiple venue) of all time – and left with an updated collection, new friends and a world record title!

news.title: FIFA Under Fire Over Plan To Sell World Cup Stake To Joshua Kushner Investment Firm
news.lede: Controversial plans to sell stakes in the FIFA World Cup to private investors have sparked a furious response from football authorities and politicians. UEFA, the body that governs European football, took the unprecedented step of releasing a statement condemning FIFA’s plan, which involves creating a new entity that would house the commercial rights to its men’s and women’s tournaments. The World Cup “is not FIFA’s to sell,” said UEFA. JP Morgan Chase, the bank that financed the failed breakaway European Super League in 2021, is working with FIFA to create the business, which is being valued at around $20B, per various reports.

news.title: Dangerous development: European nations threaten to boycott the World Cup
news.lede: A sharp dispute has erupted between the bodies responsible for football around the world, against the backdrop of plans by the International Federation of Association Football, "FIFA", to attract private investment in the World Cup. UEFA have reacted furiously, and the crisis has now reached the point of threats to boycott the tournament. FIFA had announced a plan to launcha new entity, with the aim of merging the sale of its commercial rights, which include broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing, with the operational management of organising its tournaments. Under the proposed plan, the international federation is seeking to raise up to 4.2 billion dollars from outside investors, through the sale of non-controlling minority stakes in the new entity, which is valued at around 20 billion dollars.

news.title: Jared Kushner's Brother Is Poised to Lead a $20 Billion FIFA World Cup Venture That Has UEFA Furious: 'No
news.lede: FIFA’s plan to build a $20 billion commercial company around the World Cup has pulled the Kushner family into a political controversy, with Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Eternal expected to lead a private investor group and UEFA warning that football’s "soul and governance" are not for sale. What's in FIFA's $20 Billion Proposal? The proposal would create FIFA Forward Enterprise, or FFE, to manage commercial and event operations for the World Cup, Club World Cup and other competitions. FIFA wants to raise as much as $4.2 billion by selling minority, non-controlling stakes based on a $20 billion valuation.

news.title: FIFA Faces Revolt Over $20B World Cup Sell-Off Plan
news.lede: World soccer governing body FIFA and its controversial CEO Gianni Infantino are under fire over plans to sell off a stake in FIFA’s commercial operations to private equity investors. The plan would see FIFA set up a new entity, called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), that would bundle all the money-making operations associated with the soccer World Cup — including broadcast rights, sponsorship, ticket sales and licensing fees — and sell a significant stake in the new operation to private investors. FIFA is valuing the new commercial venture at around $20 billion. After news of the plan broke on Tuesday, FIFA confirmed it is working with U.S. investment bank JP Morgan to set up the new entity.
